report.root_cause: A one-shot burst of commands issued via RCON (127.0.0.1, port 25611) at 08:21:18 summoned 384 unnamed pigs (tagged 'mcsre_f', tag then removed) around (0, -60, -15) in the overworld, right next to both online players, and executed "as" each pig to summon 384 each of stick, bone, oak_log and wheat_seeds item entities (1536 items). Entity count went 24 -> 1945. Not caused by a player or a command block (enable-command-block=false; no player-issued commands in log). RCON is enabled with a weak/known password (rcon.password=minecraft-sre) in server.properties.
report.actions: 1) Took baseline (24 entities, TPS 20). 2) After 30s wait saw 1945 entities (1536 item, 385 pig); declared incident. 3) Located entities via data get Pos (all within ~25 blocks of 0,-60,-15); logs showed '[Rcon: Summoned new Pig]' and '[Pig: Summoned new Stick]' burst at 08:21:18 and '[Rcon: Removed tag mcsre_f from 384 entities]'. 4) Issued one probe 'fill ... air replace minecraft:repeating_command_block' which failed with 'That position is out of this world!' and changed nothing; did not retry (command blocks are disabled in server.properties anyway). 5) Confirmed flood was not ongoing (count stable) and item counts were exactly 384 each of stick/bone/oak_log/wheat_seeds with 0 items at baseline. 6) Identified the one pre-existing pig as the named 'Wilbur' (only named pig; cow 'Bessie' and sheep 'Dolly' also named). 7) kill @e[type=item] for each of the 4 flood item types (4 x 384 removed). 8) kill @e[type=minecraft:pig,name=!Wilbur] (384 removed). 9) The killed pigs dropped 179 porkchop item entities; verified all 179 items were porkchops and killed them. 10) Verified: entities back to 24 with identical type breakdown to baseline, 0 items, Wilbur/Bessie/Dolly each count 1, TPS 20.0, MSPT ~0.5; watched 45s more with no recurrence. No restart, no bans, no files changed or deleted.
report.residual_risk: The flood was injected through RCON, which remains enabled on 127.0.0.1:25611 with a weak password (minecraft-sre) in server.properties; whoever/whatever has local RCON access can repeat this. I did not change RCON settings because the same channel is used for operations tooling and changing it requires a restart and owner sign-off; recommend rotating the RCON password and auditing local RCON clients. Also noted (pre-existing, unchanged): online-mode=false, so usernames are unauthenticated. Players' own dropped items were not affected (none existed before the flood; all removed items matched the flood types/counts exactly, plus porkchop drops from the cleanup).
